GeoIntel: storyboard

The app in fourteen frames, from the live globe to a phone. Each frame is a real screenshot of the running app on sample data.

14 frames, about 86 seconds at the timings given.

See what is happening

Frame 1 of 14 · 6 s

The live globe

On screen

Events from the news feed as pins on a globe, with the ranked list beside it. Filters for time, scope and severity sit above the list.

Narration

“Every event the news is reporting, placed on the map and ranked by how serious it is.”

Frame 2 of 14 · 5 s

Open an event

On screen

Clicking an event opens its analysis: severity, scope, country and type at a glance, with a link to the country.

Narration

“Pick any event and its analysis opens beside the map.”

Frame 3 of 14 · 8 s

One development, many stories

On screen

Twelve stories from twelve outlets about the same development are grouped into one. The most reported headline leads, the other angles are listed, and casualty figures are quoted as whole sentences with their sources.

Narration

“Duplicate coverage is folded into one situation, so you read the development once, with every source named.”

Understand the place

Frame 4 of 14 · 7 s

A country, in numbers

On screen

The country analysis has six tabs. Economy shows each figure with its year, its rank among 214 countries and its long-run trend.

Narration

“Click a country for the numbers behind it: where it ranks, and how it has changed since 1991.”

Weather and time

Frame 5 of 14 · 6 s

Weather layers

On screen

Weather mode with the Layers menu open: live radar and clouds, and forecast maps for temperature, pressure, rain and wind, each labelled as a model, not observed.

Narration

“Switch to Weather for live radar and satellite clouds, and forecast layers clearly marked as forecasts.”

Frame 6 of 14 · 6 s

A storm, with its forecast

On screen

A cyclone selected from the live hazard list: its alert level, intensity, dates and track, with the temperature forecast drawn underneath and its legend.

Narration

“Hazards come with their alert level and track, on top of the forecast you chose.”

Frame 7 of 14 · 6 s

Time zones, honestly

On screen

Time Zone mode: a zone clicked on the globe shows its clock changes, the sun at that point and the rules; a city is pinned to the world clock.

Narration

“Click anywhere to see the local time, when the clocks last and next change, and where the sun is.”

What it could mean

Frame 8 of 14 · 8 s

Cascade: who is exposed

On screen

A closure of the Strait of Hormuz, run from the Cascade button in Events mode: countries coloured by exposure (red High, orange Moderate, yellow Low), with a key and a way back to the result.

Narration

“Ask what happens if a route closes, and see who is exposed, coloured on the map.”

Frame 9 of 14 · 8 s

Every colour shows its evidence

On screen

The result lists each country with its mechanism and how soon it bites. Opening Why shows the figures and their source, for example how much of its gas a country imports and how much comes from the trigger country.

Narration

“Nothing is a guess: each country opens to the figures and sources behind its colour.”

Stay informed

Frame 10 of 14 · 7 s

Choose your own alerts

On screen

A watched place with its alert choices: which hazards, a minimum level, situations or serious events inside the radius, weather limits and clock changes.

Narration

“Watch the places you care about and choose exactly which alerts each one raises.”

Frame 11 of 14 · 5 s

Settings in one place

On screen

The Dashboard holds Saved, Sources, Watchlist, Alerts and Settings: units, clocks, map style, alert emails and sign out. Choices are remembered on the device.

Narration

“Display choices, alert emails and sign out live together in the dashboard.”

On the go

Frame 12 of 14 · 4 s

On a phone: the menu

On screen

The three modes sit in a menu; Draw, Layers and the Dashboard stay in the top bar.

Narration

“On a phone the modes fold into a menu, and the tools stay one tap away.”

Frame 13 of 14 · 5 s

On a phone: the map

On screen

The same Cascade result on a phone: the key moves to the top so it never covers the List and Details buttons.

Narration

“The map and its key are laid out for a thumb.”

Frame 14 of 14 · 5 s

On a phone: Cascade

On screen

The Cascade panel full width: pick what happens and where, run it, save it or ask for a written summary, all from a phone.

Narration

“And the full Cascade workspace fits in your hand.”
